subjects.displayTitle: The Bayan: promise, fulfilment, and changing law
subjects.introduction: Bahá’u’lláh says He did not abrogate the Bayán but came to it as morning dew to what had been sown. The image refuses the simple opposition between keeping and discarding, and it frames a harder question: how can a revelation fulfil a book while changing its laws? The Báb called His own Bayán a ring on the hand of Him Whom God shall make manifest, to be turned as He pleases, and warned His followers not to be veiled by the Bayán from the One it announced; yet, Bahá’u’lláh observes, many were veiled a myriad times. The Kitáb-i-Aqdas is the governing book for Bahá’ís, preserving Bayánic laws where it confirms them, and ‘Abdu’l-Bahá worries that a premature translation of the Bayán would lead readers to mistake severe abrogated laws for the basis of the Faith. Qur’an 2:106, on replacing one verse with a better or similar one, invites comparison of divine authority over revelation without assuming the two accounts are identical [1]. The way continues toward He Whom God shall make manifest, toward the Báb’s own station and claims, and toward the responsible publication of the Sacred Writings.
subjects.arc: Begin with fulfilment as nourishment, trace the Bayan’s orientation toward the promised Manifestation, and then distinguish legal continuity, abrogation, and responsible presentation.

order.why: Open with the morning dew nourishing the earlier sowing.
Hear the Point of the Bayan call for words of renewed grace.
Read the image of a ring held in the hand of the promised One.
shortened: For all that hath been exalted in the Bayan is but as a ring upon My hand, and I Myself am, verily, but a ring upon the hand of Him Whom God shall make manifest --  glorified be His mention! He turneth it as He pleaseth, for whatsoever He pleaseth, and through whatsoever He pleaseth.

order.why: Consider the Bayan as a leaf dependent upon acceptance.
shortened: Consider ye, then recall what the Point of the Bayan hath spoken concerning this Revelation, saying "Verily, I am the first to worship Him." The station of the Book, the Mother Book, the Tablet and the Preserved Tablet hath been and is manifest and evident. He saith that the Bayan and whatsoever hath been revealed therein is but a leaf among the leaves of His Paradise and is dependent upon His acceptance.

order.why: Identify the book’s function as a herald.
Read remembrance and recognition as its purpose.
Attend to the Bayan’s own account of its ordered chapters.
Read the devotional acknowledgement of its establishment.
Keep the preservation of the Bayan within the stated horizon of the next Resurrection.
shortened: O God! Preserve everyone who preserves the Bayan with all its letters, even to a single point, and cast away anyone who casts away the Bayan, even if his veiling be from a single point thereof, and he fails to preserve it, for this is Thy sustenance for all Thy creation until the next Resurrection.

order.why: Retain the earlier letter’s instruction about the maturity of the Cause.
Read the attributed explanation of accommodation and new disclosure.
Consider the new resurrection and the relation of ordinances to recognition.
shortened: You have not yet comprehended the new resurrection, the new spirit, and the new words. The Cause of the Bayan is sanctified above those matters that have passed away. What was with you before has been rolled up, and a new carpet has been spread by leave of God, the Most High, the Most Manifest.

Today all the divine names have returned to their kingdom, and none comprehend this save those possessed of certitude and insight. Whatever hath been revealed in the Bayan, whether of ordinances or attributes pertaining to the Letters and Mirrors, profiteth no one except through recognition of this Manifestation.

order.why: Follow the claim that the former revelation requires recognition of the new.
shortened: What was revealed in the Bayan sufficeth you not today except through this Revelation, at whose appearance the Cock of the Throne crowed and the Tongue of Grandeur proclaimed: "The Kingdom belongeth unto God, the One, the All-Powerful, the All-Forgiving!"

order.why: Examine using a promised book to reject its claimed fulfilment.
shortened: We sent down the Bayan and made it glad tidings for mankind lest they stray from the path. But when the promise came to pass and the Promised One appeared, they turned away save those on whose faces thou seest the radiance of divine bounty. When it is said to them "By what proof did ye believe in God?" they say "The Bayan." Yet when its Revealer came to them they denied the All-Merciful.

order.why: Consider neglect of the law pertaining to the Manifestation.
Read the reported warning against allowing the Bayanic Unity to become a veil.
shortened: God explicitly states in the Qur'an that two calls follow in succession, and the Bab--may my spirit be a sacrifice unto Him--rent asunder all the veils of the people and set no condition for the appearance of Him Whom God shall make manifest, declaring "Should He appear this very moment, I would be the first to adore Him," and explicitly stating: "Beware, beware lest thou be veiled by the Bayanic Unity or by what hath been revealed in the Bayan."
Yet now the people of the Bayan are veiled a myriad times from the Sun of Truth.

order.why: Keep the warning against measuring the new Manifestation by the former book.
shortened: Doth it beseem anyone to cling to the Bayan in his turning away from God, or to use it as proof when the All-Merciful hath come with His mighty kingdom?
Say: Fear God, and weigh Him not by the Bayan. God hath made it but a leaf among the leaves of the garden of His presence, were ye of the fair-minded.

order.why: Read the limits placed upon allusion and prior description.
Return to the worth ascribed to one word of the new revelation.
shortened: The Beloved of creation declares: One word from the Divine Word in that Most Great Manifestation is better than all that was revealed in the Bayan.

order.why: Consider the authority claimed to change an ordinance.
Introduce the Kitab-i-Aqdas and the Book of the Covenant.
shortened: The Book that abrogates all previous scriptures and books is the Most Holy Book, which is the foundation of the Preserved Tablet of the Covenant, and the Book of the Covenant is its interpreter and expositor.

order.why: State the distinction between abrogated laws and those confirmed.
Explains the authority to reveal and abrogate ordinances and answers objections from adherents of the Bayan.
Retain the concise repetition of that distinction.
Distinguish abrogation from an explanatory alteration.
Read the identification of the book binding upon Baha’is.
Keep the further clarification of that reference point.
Consider the concrete example of greetings that were retained.
shortened: These four greetings are from the commandments of His Holiness the Exalted One (may my spirit be a sacrifice for Him) and have not been abrogated, and you have not acted contrary to the Law of God.

order.why: Read the passage on hospitality, clothing, and refinement within its source limits.
Keep the severe characterization of Bayanic laws as an attributed argument.
Read the polemical distinction alongside its positive account of love and civic loyalty.
Consider the historical concern about how translation could misrepresent the applicable laws.
shortened: As regards the translation and publication of the Bayan, there are laws in the Bayan which have been abrogated by the Kitab-i-Aqdas and the Baha'is are bound by the laws of the Kitab-i-Aqdas. Were the Bayan to be published and translated, the peoples of the other countries -- and indeed even the Persians -- would think that the basis of the religion of the Baha'is was those severe laws which are found in the Bayan. Whereas according to the explicit text of the Kitab-i-Aqdas those laws are not applicable.

order.why: Read the further instruction about translation in that setting.
Close with the supplied passage on acceptance and the joy of revelation.

questions: How does the image of morning dew help us think about continuity between revelations?
What distinction do these passages draw between the Bayan’s purpose and the continued applicability of its individual laws?
How might attachment to a sacred book support recognition, and how might it obstruct it?
What does Quran 2:106 contribute to comparison of authority and change, and what questions does that comparison leave open?
How should the historical setting of severe polemical passages and publication instructions influence their presentation to new readers?

neighbors.invitation: Consider how translation and publication shape readers’ understanding.

references.label: 1 · Quran 2:106 · Replacement and divine authority
references.note: The verse speaks of replacing or setting aside a verse or sign with one better or similar, grounding this in divine power. Compare its language with the compilation’s distinction between spiritual fulfilment and changed ordinances. This comparison does not assume that Islamic accounts of abrogation and Baha’i accounts of successive revelations are identical.

subjects.displayTitle: Guardianship: a charge of fidelity and defined authority
subjects.introduction: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá, looking at a grandson of eleven or twelve, is remembered calling him His future Elisha and seeing in his eyes not a conqueror but an abyss of fidelity, endurance and conscientiousness. That office was then set down in writing. The Will and Testament names Shoghi Effendi the Guardian of the Cause of God and the expounder of its words, and places him together with the Universal House of Justice under the unerring guidance promised to both. From that follows a set of careful boundaries: the Guardian interprets, the House of Justice legislates, and neither invades the other’s sphere; his infallibility belongs to his function, and his personal letters are counsel rather than pronouncements. When his ministry ended without a successor, the House of Justice warned against two opposite errors, treating the Guardianship as a dead letter and straining the clear texts to produce a Guardian. The mantle that fell from Elijah to Elisha offers an image of continuity and calling, though not of an authority the Bahá’í texts define for themselves [1]. The journey continues toward authoritative interpretation and its limits, the twin pillars of this Order, and the Hands of the Cause with their own charge of protection.
subjects.arc: Enter through a remembered encounter, turn to the written provisions and their authority, then study the institutional distinctions and the later response to loss.

order.why: Turn to the written testament and its extensive provisions.
shortened: O my loving friends! After the passing away of this wronged one, it is incumbent upon the Aghsan (Branches), the Afnan (Twigs) of the Sacred Lote-Tree, the Hands (pillars) of the Cause of God and the loved ones of the Abha Beauty to turn unto Shoghi Effendi--the youthful branch branched from the two hallowed and sacred Lote-Trees and the fruit grown from the union of the two offshoots of the Tree of Holiness,--as he is the sign of God, the chosen branch, the Guardian of the Cause of God, he unto whom all the Aghsan, the Afnan, the Hands of the Cause of God and His loved ones must turn. He is the expounder of the words of God and after him will succeed the first-born of his lineal descendents.

The sacred and youthful branch, the Guardian of the Cause of God, as well as the Universal House of Justice, to be universally elected and established, are both under the care and protection of the Abha Beauty, under the shelter and unerring guidance of the Exalted One (may my life be offered up for them both). Whatsoever they decide is of God.

order.why: Open with the reported encounter with the young Shoghi Effendi, clearly retaining its status as recollection.
shortened: As usual we silently waited for Him to address us, which He soon did: "Well, my daughter", the Master commenced, "how do you like Shoghi Effendi, my future Elisha?" (Old Testament, 2 Kings, 2nd chapter, verse 13). "Master, if I may speak frankly, then I have to say that in his boyish face are the dark eyes of a sufferer, of one who will suffer a lot!"

Thoughtfully the Master looked beyond us into a far distance, only after a considerable time did His glance come back to us, and He said: "My grandson does not have the eyes of a pioneer, of a fighter, of a victor, but in his eyes, in his glances there is an abyss (=depth) of fidelity, endurance and conscientiousness.

Long pause! - Then 'Abbas Effendi - 'Abdu'l-Baha rose and said in a firm voice in a solemn tone: "I am not giving my Elisha to the British to educate, I dedicate and give him to the All-Highest. God's eyes will keep watch over my child in Oxford also. - Insha'allah."

order.why: Compare the reported account of custodianship and care for the shrines.
Keep the further reported statement distinct from the testament itself.
Retain the letter about consent and the keeping of correspondence without attributing an unstated connection.
A playful personal address to Shoghi urging memorization and chanting of prayers.
Begin the supplied readings with the account of the twin successors.
Distinguish interpretation from legislation.
shortened: From these statements it is made indubitably clear and evident that the Guardian of the Faith has been made the Interpreter of the Word and that the Universal House of Justice has been invested with the function of legislating on matters not expressly revealed in the teachings.
Neither can, nor will ever, infringe upon the sacred and prescribed domain of the other. Neither will seek to curtail the specific and undoubted authority with which both have been divinely invested.

order.why: Consider powers exercised within prescribed limits.
Read the Guardianship as supporting the House of Justice’s own authority.
shortened: It must be also clearly understood by every believer that the institution of Guardianship does not under any circumstances abrogate, or even in the slightest degree detract from, the powers granted to the Universal House of Justice by Baha'u'llah in the "Kitabu'l-Aqdas," and repeatedly and solemnly confirmed by 'Abdu'l-Baha in His Will.

It enhances the prestige of that exalted assembly, stabilizes its supreme position, safeguards its unity, assures the continuity of its labors, without presuming in the slightest to infringe upon the inviolability of its clearly defined sphere of jurisdiction.

order.why: Examine the explicit limit concerning exclusive legislation.
Consider the passage on the interdependence of the two institutions.
Read the explanation of the scope of infallibility.
Distinguish the Guardian from the perfect exemplar.
Keep the concise pilgrim-note answer visibly separate from authoritative explanations.
Consider responsibility for defining matters requiring obedience.
Read the concern about bickering and opinionatedness.
Distinguish elucidating interpretations from changing temporary rulings.
Consider the status of letters written through secretaries.
Read the stated audience and intended use of personal letters.
Distinguish fidelity to the original from improvement of translations.
Hear the translator’s humility concerning a befitting rendering.
Consider administration before the formation of the Universal House of Justice.
Read the later determination that a second Guardian could not be appointed.
Acknowledge the loss while considering the continuing Covenant.
Examine the warning against two opposite conclusions from the absence of a living Guardian.
shortened: The Guardianship does not lose its significance nor position in the Order of Baha'u'llah merely because there is no living Guardian. We must guard against two extremes: one is to argue that because there is no Guardian all that was written about the Guardianship and its position in the Baha'i World Order is a dead letter and was unimportant; the other is to be so overwhelmed by the significance of the Guardianship as to underestimate the strength of the Covenant, or to be tempted to compromise with the clear texts in order to find somehow, in some way, a Guardian.

order.why: Read the clarification concerning the House of Justice’s proper sphere.
Consider the continuing role of the Guardian’s writings in legislation.
Keep the limit on authoritative interpretation explicit.
Read the statement concerning the headship of the Faith.
End with the development of an institution for continuing service and coordination.
shortened: The time is indeed propitious for the establishment of the International Teaching Centre, a development which, at one and the same time, brings to fruition the work of the Hands of the Cause residing in the Holy Land and provides for its extension into the future, links the institution of the Boards of Counsellors even more intimately with that of the Hands of the Cause of God, and powerfully reinforces the discharge of the rapidly growing responsibilities of the Universal House of Justice.
All the Hands of the Cause of God will be members of the International Teaching Centre.

questions: How do the recollections, testamentary provisions, and later explanatory letters contribute differently to understanding the Guardianship?
Why do the distinctions between interpretation and legislation matter for the relationships described here?
What does a defined sphere of infallibility imply, and how is it distinguished from omniscience or perfect exemplarity?
How do the later letters address the relationship between an institution’s enduring significance and the absence of a living officeholder?
What does the narrative of Elijah and Elisha illuminate about fidelity and succession, and where does that analogy reach its limits?
How might these readings shape careful use of personal correspondence, translations, and reported conversations?

neighbors.invitation: Explore the distinct responsibilities of interpretation and legislation.

references.label: 1 · 2 Kings 2:9–15 · Elisha takes up Elijah’s mantle
references.note: Elisha asks for a share in Elijah’s spirit, witnesses his departure, and takes up his mantle; others then recognize the spirit of Elijah resting upon him. Read this narrative beside the Elisha allusion in the reported childhood encounter. The imagery concerns continuity and calling, while the Baha’i institution’s authority is specified by its own texts.

subjects.displayTitle: Ages of promise, renewal, and human maturity
subjects.introduction: This is the springtime of the Eternal One, ‘Abdu’l-Bahá announces, and He immediately says what such a season is for: universal peace, a common language, the union of religions, and friends whose only weapons are reconciliation and speech. The long view of religious history serves that near purpose. He explains that every religion has carried two kinds of law, the ethical foundation unchanged from the dawn of the Adamic cycle, and the social ordinances that each age renews; that a universal cycle spans countless ages until one supreme Manifestation brings the world to maturity; and that the cycle which began with Adam has reached that point in Bahá’u’lláh, under whose shadow future Messengers will still appear. The Báb counts the years differently, so the terms cycle, dispensation, age and epoch repay careful sorting before any timeline is drawn. Krishna’s promise to appear whenever righteousness declines offers a separate account of renewal [1]. The journey leads on into the coming of age and maturity of mankind, into the cycles of the physical and spiritual worlds, and into the future divine revelations that a very long cycle still holds.
subjects.arc: Begin with springtime and its ethical possibilities, distinguish the scales and meanings of cycles, then follow the movement from revelation into sustained community building.

order.why: Read the detailed chronology and developmental imagery in its supplied form without harmonizing its claims.
shortened: Every Manifestation is the Adam of His time. (Adam means the type man, the perfect man.)
There were one hundred thousand Adams before the Adam of biblical records each being the Manifestation of His own time or cycle.
This cycle in which we are living and which has come to its full expression today having ended thus, is the long Adamic cycle, being five hundred thousand years.
Five hundred thousand years ago a Great Manifestation came and founded it.
Today, which culminates this long cycle - Baha'u'llah being, in the words of 'Abdu'l-Baha, "The expression of maturity and perfection of humanity."

He is the Founder also of the new long cycle of 500,000 years when another great Manifestation will come. In the meantime throughout this coming long cycle of 500,000 years there will be cycles like that of Moses, Jesus, etc., only on a higher scale, as this is the Kingdom of Heaven on Earth. None will be as great as Baha'u'llah until 500,000 years is accomplished.
'Abdu'l-Baha says that within the last 500,000 years there have been seven universal Manifestations, the last three of whom were Melchizedek, Jesus Christ, and Baha'u'llah.

order.why: Open with the image of a new spiritual spring.
shortened: This is the age of the Blessed Perfection and this is the time of the Greatest Name! This is the century of the Manifestation, the age of the Sun of all horizons and the beautiful springtime of the Eternal One!

order.why: Give the cycle’s promise concrete expressions in peace and fellowship.
shortened: Glad tidings of the Kingdom of Abha! We announce to you glad tidings of great joy! Similar words were spoken almost two thousand years ago. Reflect and be not of the heedless. This is the great day of God. This is the day of universal peace, of universal brotherhood, of a universal language and of the union of all religions. This is the day wherein the prophecies of the Holy Books of every tongue have been or are being fulfilled. This is the cycle of Baha'u'llah.

order.why: Read its distinctive instruments as reason, love, and peaceful utterance.
shortened: In this Most Great Cycle, the suckling child has the station of a noble person, and newborn children are wise, seeing and praiseworthy. For the Lord God has manifested Himself through His attribute of the All-Merciful and educates humanity with utmost love.
Neither sword nor arrow exists, nor blade nor instrument of iron. The weapons of the divine friends are peace and reconciliation, and their world-conquering sword is utterance, expression and speech.

order.why: Connect the age with unity and harmony.
Establish the enduring ethical foundation across religions.
Consider the different requirements of a new age.
Distinguish changing material ordinances from enduring foundations.
Read the account of universal cycles and future Manifestations.
Compare the reported account of earlier universal cycles.
Retain the Bab’s account of a cycle and its distinct span of time.
shortened: And this cycle of Manifestation -- which extendeth from the Dispensation of Adam, peace be upon Him, until this day, a span of twelve thousand two hundred and ten solar years -- hath, in every age, appeared under a distinct Name.

order.why: Consider the symbolic rank and expansive language of the cycle.
Read the description of its relation to earlier manifestations.
Keep the reported distinction among dispensations.
shortened: Most blessed are you because you are living in the Cycle of His Highness the Desired One!

This Cycle is the Cycle of the Blessed Perfection. Each one of the prophets had a Dispensation. Thus we have the Dispensation of Moses, the Cycle of Christ, the epiphany of Mohamad. But this Cycle is the Cycle of the Blessed Perfection.

order.why: Hear the announcement of another cycle.
shortened: Say: O people! Another cycle hath come and the All-Merciful hath appeared with great sovereignty.

order.why: A short question and answer about the future beyond the Bahai cycle and the endless outpouring of divine bounties.
Retain the concise naming of a divine age.
Consider the century as a period of unfolding signs.
shortened: For a century spans one hundred years, so in this glorious age of the Majestic Lord, day by day the Divine Cause rises higher and more exalted, more sublime and unreachable. The manifestation of the signs of beauty and glory and the appearance of the tokens of might and greatness of the peerless Lord continue.

order.why: Read the reported expectation of wider influence.
shortened: As this century is the century of light and the Cycle of the revelation of Mysteries undoubtedly these glorious aims will be fully established and the influence of this great Cause will encircle the East and the West."

order.why: Connect the new age with gifts and outpourings.
shortened: All these outpourings are from the grace and bounty of the Sovereign of existence, which in this new age and wondrous century have been bestowed upon the loved ones of the All-Merciful.

order.why: Pause at the description of bounty and joy.
shortened: The cycle of the Greatest Name is bounty upon bounty and joy upon joy.

order.why: Read gratitude for participation in the age.
Consider receiving a share of its gifts.
Move from historical vision into prayer for embodied unity.
Let the horizon enlarge hope and aspiration.
shortened: O thou lamp of the gathering of the love of God!

In this Most Great Cycle wherein the weakest of souls, through the power of divine bestowal, are adorned with the robe of "He strengtheneth whom He willeth with His strength" and wherein the servants of the Most Glorious Threshold are invested with the robe of "Thou givest sovereignty to whom Thou willest" and the garment of "He singles out for His mercy whomsoever He pleaseth" - one must make hope powerful and aspiration lofty and noble.

order.why: Read the summons to active service.
shortened: O Samandar, Fire ignited by the divine! In this Most Great Cycle and century of the Sovereign King of Eternity, souls are confirmed and assisted by the hosts of the Abha Kingdom such that, like armies of power and might, they storm forth in the arena of diffusing the divine fragrances and strive to exalt the Word of God.

order.why: Consider the demand to become signs of guidance.
Close the linked readings with generosity toward other peoples.
shortened: In this Most Great Century and Most Noble Cycle, when subtle and pure realities have been illumined by the shining rays from the Sun of Truth, and when the temples of unity have been raised up in the arena of existence through this perfect bounty and all-encompassing grace, the souls who are ready must count as a precious gift this glorious favor and mighty grace, and in this Most Great Cycle, having been illumined by the lights of the manifestation of the Ancient Sun, they must bestow bounty and generosity upon other peoples from the Orient of the world.

order.why: Begin the supplied accounts with the broad outline of Heroic and Formative ages.
Read the division of the Heroic Age into epochs.
Consider the testament as a link between ages.
shortened: It was 'Abdu'l-Baha Who, through the provisions of His weighty Will and Testament, has forged the vital link which must for ever connect the age that has just expired with the one we now live in -- the Transitional and Formative period of the Faith -- a stage that must in the fullness of time reach its blossom and yield its fruit in the exploits and triumphs that are to herald the Golden Age of the Revelation of Baha'u'llah.

order.why: Follow the transition from foundational lives toward institutions.
shortened: The Formative Period, the Iron Age, of that Dispensation was now beginning, the Age in which the institutions, local, national and international, of the Faith of Baha'u'llah were to take shape, develop and become fully consolidated, in anticipation of the third, the last, the Golden Age destined to witness the emergence of a world-embracing Order enshrining the ultimate fruit of God's latest Revelation to mankind, a fruit whose maturity must signalize the establishment of a world civilization and the formal inauguration of the Kingdom of the Father upon earth as promised by Jesus Christ Himself.

order.why: Keep the dated explanation of epochs within its historical setting.
Consider the Iron Age as a metaphor for labour and construction.
Read the later account of three stages as an integrated whole.
Connect the Guardian’s work with the development of elected institutions.
End with the supplied account of collective effort across peoples.

questions: What qualities of life are associated with the arrival of a spiritual spring in these selections?
How do enduring ethical foundations and changing social ordinances relate to one another?
What distinctions among cycle, dispensation, age, and epoch seem necessary before drawing a chronology?
How does the Gita’s connection between divine manifestation and the renewal of righteousness compare with the purposes described here?
How might a long view of human maturity strengthen practical effort without encouraging complacency about present suffering?

neighbors.invitation: Ask what the maturity of humanity would require in practice.

references.label: 1 · Bhagavad Gita 4:7 · Divine appearance and the renewal of righteousness
references.note: Krishna connects divine manifestation with a decline in righteousness and a rise in its opposite. Compare this with the compilation’s concern for recurring renewal and the development of human capacities. The verse’s account of divine appearance has its own theological setting; it is not a matching chronology of Baha’i cycles. Translation by Swami Mukundananda.

subjects.displayTitle: Victory through words, deeds, and reconciliation
subjects.introduction: One pure deed, Bahá’u’lláh declares, outweighs the victory of an army fighting in the path of God. With that measure the meaning of religious triumph changes: the law of holy war is blotted from the Book, the sword of the tongue is to be drawn instead of steel, and weapons are to become means of peace. The vocabulary of conquest survives, but it now names the winning of hearts, and the reader must watch how the same words shift their sense. Historical and reported discussions remain: the Báb’s earlier treatment of jihad, accounts of why Moses and Muhammad were permitted to fight for the protection of their followers, warnings that the fervour of a declared holy war escapes the control of those who proclaim it. Qur’an 22:39, which grants permission to those who have been wronged, offers a focused comparison for these discussions of defence [1]. The way forward runs through war and peace, through the fanaticism and hatred that make bloodshed possible, and into the inward struggle where the only sanctioned warfare is waged against the self.
subjects.arc: Begin with a pure deed outweighing military victory, establish the prohibition on religious warfare, examine the historical arguments, and return to the work of reconciliation.

order.why: Read the transformation from a physical sword to utterance.
Open with the greater victory of a pure deed.
shortened: The triumph of a single pure deed is, in the sight of God, greater than the victory of an army that striveth in the path of God, for the shedding of blood is not beloved, and in this Most Great Revelation, victory hath been ordained through word and utterance.

order.why: Hear abolition of holy war announced as glad tidings.
Connect the prohibition of bloodshed with harmony and unity.
Read the substitution of persuasive utterance for the sword.
shortened: Know thou that We have annulled the rule of the sword, as an aid to Our Cause, and substituted for it the power born of the utterance of men. Thus have We irrevocably decreed, by virtue of Our grace.

order.why: Address the request for weapons through that same transformation.
Consider weapons transformed into means of peace.
Read the sword image redirected toward loving-kindness.
Examine misunderstandings of victory beside kindness and care.
Connect assistance to the prohibition of strife.
Retain the concise declaration that the decree is erased.
shortened: The decree of holy war and strife hath been erased from the Book by the finger of divine power.

order.why: Explicitly abolishes holy war and contrasts earlier restrictions with fellowship and freedom in the present Revelation.
Read the account of the Ridvan announcements.
shortened: On the first day when the Ancient Beauty was seated upon the Most Great Throne in the garden named Ridvan, the tongue of grandeur spoke three verses: First, that the sword is abolished in this Revelation; second, that before the completion of a thousand years, whosoever makes a claim is false, and the year is a complete year - interpretation and explanation of this verse are forbidden; and third, that God, exalted be His glory, at that moment shed the radiance of all His names upon all things.

order.why: Place the changed ordinance within successive revelations.
Preserve the Bab’s earlier treatment of jihad in its own setting.
Read the explanation of practices in the early days of the Cause.
shortened: Question: Can you provide an account of Tahirih's deliverance from Qazvin, her arrival in Tihran, her departure for Badasht, and the events that transpired there?

Answer: In brief, what happened is the following. Those were the early days of the Cause and no one was informed of the divine teachings. All followed the law of the Qur'an and regarded warfare, retribution, and retaliation as permissible.

order.why: Attend to the recurring human cost of conflict.
shortened: This Wronged One observed that every year warfare and conflict would arise between the Babi and Shi'ih parties, with many slain on both sides.

order.why: Consider the account of prohibiting strife after departure to Iraq.
shortened: All know that previously, every year witnessed strife and conflict, with many souls slain on both sides - one year in Tabarsi, another in Zanjan, another in Nayriz. But after this Wronged One's departure to Iraq, by permission of His Majesty the Sultan, We forbade all from corruption and strife. If thou deniest this, the world beareth witness, though certain slanderers and deniers have concealed the good deeds of the Most Exalted Pen and spoken and continue to speak according to their desires. But by the life of God! Baha speaketh not from desire, but rather uttereth that which draweth mankind unto the Most Sublime Horizon.

order.why: Keep the historical and polemical comparison attributed while noting its explicit rejection of those actions now.
shortened: The Seal of the Prophets commanded that in three days seven hundred souls be put to death, and 'Ali and Zubayr beheaded them. And were all those who were slain as mentioned in the Qur'an to be recorded, all would be seized with wonderment. Consider in the Bayanic Dispensation how many souls were consigned to perdition. In every city they killed and were killed.
But this Wronged One, by God's command, hath removed these things and strictly forbidden them in His Books, His Scriptures and His Tablets.

order.why: Read the reported account of defensive warfare.
Keep the longer reported comparison of Moses, Christ, and Muhammad in its historical register.
shortened: When and where it was necessary, God told Moses to conquer his enemies who came up to destroy him and the Israelites. Christ lived only three years of His ministry, but as He came to prepare the world for the coming of God, He lived until His mission was accomplished. He had only twelve apostles, and about seventy followers in all who believed in Him at that time, but Mohammed had thousands, and as they had only to hear him to be induced to believe, the surrounding nations threatened to destroy him and his people; so he was compelled to fight to save himself and his followers from destruction.

order.why: Consider the reported argument concerning protection and its tensions.
shortened: At the time of Muhammad, He sanctioned war for the preservation of the lives of His followers.

He commanded His followers to carry the Religion of God by the sword. When a man is about to take poison, it is right to dash the cup from his hand even with extreme violence. It will inflict injury but at the same time save his life. There must be a law to prevent the wolves , from destroying the lambs at such a period of religious history. That is why the Shepherd sanctioned such vigorous protection for the sheep.

order.why: Compare the report that rejects force as a means of spreading faith.
shortened: No Divine Messenger ever encouraged strife, or suggested that the sword be used in promulgating his teachings. When followers of Christ or Mahomet have resorted to this means of spreading their faith, imagining that they were justified by the words of their Master, they have mistaken the symbols of his teaching for its reality and have done that which he had, in fact, forbidden.

order.why: Ask whether coerced profession can produce enduring faith.
Read the reported warning about religious fervour escaping restraint.
shortened: The law of Jihad has ever been a veritable firebrand with which the Ulemas of Islam have threatened the world from time to time.

Once this law was promulgated by the Sheik-ol-Islam, the power of restraining the religious fury of the Moslems was entirely out of his hand. Even if he desired he could not bring down the floodgate of fanaticism, till it had spent its fury and force.

order.why: Retain the wartime report and its concern with preventing conflict.
Consider the reported challenge to the term religious war.
Read the warning about force even in a claimed good cause.
Distinguish willingness to suffer from willingness to kill.
Keep the account of believers’ changing response to attack as reported history.
Recognize the acknowledgement that some disobeyed the prohibition.
shortened: We forbade the servants from warfare and contention, yet some committed that which We prohibited and transgressed the bounds set by God. But God hath pardoned whom He willeth, for He is powerful over all things.

order.why: Read the consequences of failing to understand victory through expression.
shortened: By God! Victory lieth in expression, not in sword and spear, and thus have We revealed in all the Tablets, yet the people perceived it not and were among the corrupt. And thereby was shed the blood of those a single soul of whom is, in the sight of thy Lord, better than these oppressors, for they claim to believe yet slay its Establisher and Confirmer.

order.why: Turn toward the opening of spiritual conquests.
shortened: Since in this Most Great Cycle the lesser jihad of physical warfare is forbidden and condemned, therefore the doors of spiritual conquests are opened from every direction.

order.why: Retain the freedom from reliance on physical arms.
shortened: Praise be to God, there is no need for sword or spear, for the piercing blade or the strength of men's arms.

order.why: Revisit the prohibition as cited in the Epistle to the Son of the Wolf.
shortened: And yet again in another connection: "Beware lest ye shed the blood of any one. Unsheathe the sword of your tongue from the scabbard of utterance, for therewith ye can conquer the citadels of men's hearts. We have abolished the law to wage holy war against each other.

order.why: End with the reported contrast between instruments that destroy and those that give life.
shortened: Yea, in this Cause the sword is the divine fragrances. That sword killed, this one gives life; that one destroyed, this one builds; that one caused chaos, this one brings order. Great is the difference between that sword and this sword. But "God doeth whatsoever He willeth" and decrees as He desireth. At that time, such was required; now, this is what is needed. That sword conquered fortresses of stone and iron; this sword conquers fortresses and hearts. That sword spoke of divine wrath; this sword speaks of God's infinite mercy. That sword was the cause of separation and division; this sword is the cause of unity and harmony.

questions: What changes when religious victory is measured by pure deeds and the response of hearts?
How can we tell when the language of swords or conquest is being used as a spiritual image?
What do the historical discussions of defence and Quran 22:39 contribute to understanding the specific change asserted in these passages?
How do persuasion, coercion, and freely formed conviction differ in their effects on a community?
What forms of courage and discipline would be needed to make the means of religious service consistent with reconciliation?

neighbors.invitation: Follow the inquiry into the conditions of peace.

references.label: 1 · Quran 22:39 · Permission in response to wrong
references.note: The verse grants permission to fight to those who have been wronged; several translations explicitly describe them as being attacked. Read it beside the reported discussions of defensive conflict, then consider the distinct Baha’i prohibition on religious warfare. This single verse is a focused comparison, not a summary of the entire Islamic treatment of war.

subjects.displayTitle: Inheritance: freedom, family, and a wider trust
subjects.introduction: Everyone is to write a will, Bahá’u’lláh ordained, seal it, and head it with the Most Great Name; the detailed division of an estate among seven categories of heirs applies only when no will exists. That ordering puts personal intention first while urging attention to the rights of family and children. The prescribed shares, two thousand five hundred and twenty parts built on the number nine, have their own tenderness: hearing the cry of children yet unborn, Bahá’u’lláh doubled their portion; where no heir exists the estate passes to the House of Justice for orphans, widows and the common good; a minor’s share is invested by a trustworthy guardian. The daughters of Zelophehad, who asked why their father’s name should vanish for lack of a son and won a ruling that became law for all, show how one family’s question can shape a general rule [1]. The path continues into the laws of the Kitáb-i-Aqdas, the rights of the eldest son, and the law of burial that stands at the threshold of every estate.
subjects.arc: Begin with the responsibility to make a will, distinguish personal disposition from prescribed distribution, then explore particular cases and the wider meanings of inheritance.

order.why: Explains testamentary discretion, the obligation to make a clear will and the default distribution when no will applies.
Open with the distinction between a will and distribution in its absence.
shortened: As for inheritance, this distribution applies when the deceased person has not made a will - in that case this distribution takes effect. However every soul is obligated to make a will - indeed it is prescribed and mandatory. And the explicit divine texts state that in a state of health one must make a will according to wisdom, and according to their own desire they may will however they wish, and that will should be sealed and opened after their death and acted upon accordingly.

order.why: Join the freedom to revise a will with attention to family and children.
Read the affirmation of authority over one’s property.
Compare the reported explanation of freedom in making a will.
shortened: The purpose of Baha'u'llah's arrangement is that man is not to be interfered with in the leaving of his property. Man may divide his wealth as he likes. Every one has to write a will and affix a seal thereto and no one need know about the arrangement he has made. After his death the will is opened and read and whatever he has decreed will be enforced. Man should have perfect freedom to decide as he wishes, in making his will.

order.why: Keep the execution of the will prior to distribution.
Consider the importance of establishing a thoughtful practice.
Read the early example and repeated call to make a will.
Turn to the extensive ordinances, including children, trusteeship, public benefit, and the will.
shortened: We have divided inheritance into seven categories: to the children, We have allotted nine parts comprising five hundred and forty shares; to the wife, eight parts comprising four hundred and eighty shares; to the father, seven parts comprising four hundred and twenty shares; to the mother, six parts comprising three hundred and sixty shares; to the brothers, five parts or three hundred shares; to the sisters, four parts or two hundred and forty shares; and to the teachers, three parts or one hundred and eighty shares. Such was the ordinance of My Forerunner, He Who extolleth My Name in the night season and at the break of day. When We heard the clamour of the children as yet unborn, We doubled their share and decreased those of the rest. He, of a truth, hath power to ordain whatsoever He desireth, and He doeth as He pleaseth by virtue of His sovereign might.

Should the deceased leave no offspring, their share shall revert to the House of Justice, to be expended by the Trustees of the All-Merciful on the orphaned and widowed, and on whatsoever will bring benefit to the generality of the people, that all may give thanks unto their Lord, the All-Gracious, the Pardoner.

If the deceased should leave children who are under age, their share of the inheritance must be entrusted to a reliable individual, or to a company, that it may be invested on their behalf in trade and business until they come of age. The trustee should be assigned a due share of the profit that hath accrued to it from being thus employed.

order.why: Read the numerical clarification and the case of siblings.
shortened: ANSWER:  According to the Book of God, the estate of the deceased is divided into 2,520 shares, which number is the lowest common multiple of all integers up to nine, and these shares are then distributed into seven portions, each of which is allocated, as mentioned in the Book, to a particular category of heirs.  The children, for example, are allotted nine blocks of 60 shares, comprising 540 shares in all.  The meaning of the statement "We doubled their share" is thus that the children receive a further nine blocks of 60 shares, entitling them to a total of 18 blocks all told.

6. QUESTION:  Is it necessary that the brother, in order to qualify for his portion of the inheritance, be descended from both the father and the mother of the deceased, or is it sufficient merely that there be one parent in common?

ANSWER:  If the brother be descended from the father he shall receive his share of the inheritance in the prescribed measure recorded in the Book; but if he be descended from the mother, he shall receive only two thirds of his entitlement, the remaining third reverting to the House of Justice.  This ruling is also applicable to the sister.

order.why: Compare the further explanation of the children’s increased portion.
shortened: Regarding your question about inheritance, His exalted words state: "When We heard the cries of the children yet unborn, We doubled their portion and decreased from the others." The inheritances in the Divine Book are made into two thousand five hundred and twenty shares, which encompass the nine divisions. This number is divided into seven portions, each portion going to a class of heirs as mentioned in the Book.
The meaning of His exalted words "We doubled their portion" is that one equivalent was added to it, making it two "Ta," and what was increased was decreased from the others.

order.why: Preserve the fuller account of the shares and its numerical language.
shortened: The children's portion is nine-sixtieths, the spouses' portion eight-sixtieths, the fathers' portion seven-sixtieths, the mothers' portion six-sixtieths, the brothers' portion five-sixtieths, the sisters' portion four-sixtieths, and the teachers' portion three-sixtieths.

And in this Dispensation, since the Ancient Beauty, out of pure grace and bounty, has designated the children's portion, which was nine-sixtieths, to be eighteen-sixtieths, and has reduced nine-sixtieths from those other six categories, now the division must be made in this way: from each of those six categories of heirs, one and one-half sixtieths should be reduced, which totals nine-sixtieths.

order.why: Read the earlier Bayanic provision in its own theological horizon.
Consider the historical temporary provision and the future House of Justice.
shortened: In this connection, a decree was revealed in the Land of Mystery, and the portions of missing persons were temporarily assigned to existing heirs until the establishment of the House of Justice. After its establishment, its ruling shall become manifest. However, the inheritance of those who emigrated in the year in which the Ancient Beauty emigrated shall return to their heirs.

order.why: Examine cases where categories of heirs are absent.
shortened: Regarding inheritance, that if there be no offspring, their shares revert to the House of Justice, and when any of the other categories are not present, such as father, mother, brother, sister, or teacher, whether their shares also revert to the House of Justice or are otherwise disposed - this matter hath been revealed in the Book of God. He saith, exalted be He: "Should one die and leave no offspring, their share shall revert to the House of Justice" and so forth. And: "Should one leave offspring but none of the other categories specified in the Book, two-thirds of what they leave shall revert to the offspring and the remaining third to the House of Justice."

order.why: Keep the definition of parents and the referral of unspecified cases.
Read the case concerning daughters, residence, and clothing.
Consider the clarification of the eldest son.
Distinguish the residence from other houses.
Read the eldest son’s entitlement beside the call to fairness toward other heirs.
Bring attention to trustworthy custody.
Retain the priority of paying debts.
Keep the particular ruling as a specific answer.
Consider provision for the poor where there is no heir.
Read the reported proposal about workers and wealth distinctly from the enacted provisions.
Retain the passage concerning divine authority and responsibility in its supplied setting.
shortened: Say: The Lord of Command hath more authority over you than your own selves - God will judge between you with truth; woe unto you, how you fail to reflect! God hath created all that is in the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them for the Manifestation of His Self - how little do you understand! Say: All are His servants and all bow down before Him.

order.why: Turn toward a heritage of trust and resignation rather than accumulated riches.
End with the several meanings of inheritance and the transmission of divine qualities.
shortened: This much is clear, but inheritance has several meanings. One meaning is trust and submission, which is explicitly stated. Another meaning is "that which God leaveth is better for you," and a third meaning is "one who will inherit me and inherit from the family of Jacob, and make him, O my Lord, well-pleasing." And these are the divine qualities and perfections. Blessed is every heir who inherits this inheritance, for unto God belongeth the inheritance of the heavens and the earth. And whosoever inheriteth not is wronging his own soul, even if he be among the chosen ones....

questions: Why is the distinction between making a will and applying the prescribed distribution essential to reading these passages?
How do the texts bring freedom over possessions into relationship with the rights and needs of others?
What does the inclusion of teachers, trustees, and public benefit suggest about the relationships recognized here?
How does the account of Zelophehad’s daughters help us examine the relation between a particular question and a general rule?
What tensions or questions arise when we compare the specific rulings, reported proposals, and calls to fairness?
What kinds of spiritual inheritance might a person or community deliberately cultivate?

neighbors.invitation: Examine the specific provisions concerning the eldest son.

references.label: 1 · Numbers 27:1–11 · The daughters of Zelophehad ask to inherit
references.note: The daughters ask why their father’s name should disappear because he had no son. Their request is affirmed, followed by provisions for daughters and other kin when particular heirs are absent. Compare the movement from a concrete family situation to a general rule, while examining the differences between the two sets of provisions.

subjects.introduction: Still weak from a nervous fever that had left Him unable to speak or write, ‘Abdu’l-Bahá picks up His pen in Alexandria to answer a friend’s letter, apologizing for the delay. His years in Egypt, after decades of confinement in ‘Akká, appear in just such glimpses: a change of air sought for health, the climates of Port Said and Ismailia tried and found wanting, strength returning in Ramleh, visitors received, a hostile newspaper answered by a friendly one, plans adjusted when a reception turned unwelcome, and always the absent friends remembered day and night. Jesus drawing His apostles aside to rest because the coming and going left no time even to eat [1] names the same bodily cost of service. What these letters show is that resolve and acknowledged frailty can share one life, and that keeping in touch, adjusting plans and welcoming others are forms of service as real as any public address. The path leads on into ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s own narrative and autobiographical accounts, where the journeys of His later years take their place in the larger story.
subjects.arc: Begin with a reply written in convalescence, examine the journey’s purposes and constraints, then follow the relationships and hopes sustained through its changing circumstances.

order.why: Consider weakness, recovery, and the return to writing.
shortened: Due to the unsuitable climate and nervous fever each day, this earthly frame could not endure and reached the utmost weakness and decline. Therefore from arrival in Port Said until now health has been completely impaired and strength gone. However for several days in Ramleh some strength has been gained and writing is possible, so I have begun writing.

order.why: Open with the effort to answer a friend during convalescence.
Read the stated reason for a change of climate.
shortened: This letter is now being written from Alexandria, because that nervous condition which you know about has intensified in these days to such an extent that I was unable to speak or write. And since it was observed that the climate of Akka and Haifa was not agreeable in any way, so that I would not be prevented from service at the Holy Threshold and would be able to speak and write, I therefore came to these parts for a time. Praise be to God, by the favors of the Blessed Beauty, the change of climate has proven very beneficial.

order.why: Follow the specific account of unsuitable climates and convalescence.
Retain the further account of illness on the journey.
Connect a little renewed strength with correspondence.
Read writing and association during fatigue at Port Said.
Keep the particular statement of a visit for health and its restriction on teaching in that setting.
Introduce the expressed plan to visit Egypt.
shortened: In recent days, I have made a plan to visit Egypt, if this be God's will.

order.why: Read the journey as an opportunity for service.
shortened: The invisible hand has opened the doors, and wisdom requires that Abdul-Baha hasten to the country of Egypt; for he is infinitely ashamed and chagrined that he has not yet been assisted in servitude.

order.why: Hear the intention expressed on entering Egypt.
shortened: I entered the country of Egypt, trusting in God, attracted to His Kingdom, enkindled with the fire of His love, hoping that I might arise to serve at the Threshold of Glory.

order.why: Consider the hope that the journey will bear fruit.
Place that hope beside rumours and opposition.
shortened: 'Abdu'l-Baha traveled to the land of Joseph of Canaan and became renowned for servitude at the Holy Threshold. Although He is in danger from the attacks of factions and false rumors and newspaper calumnies, yet it is hoped that this journey will bear fruit and cause the fame and mention of the Cause of God to stir these regions.

order.why: Read the account of contrasting newspaper responses.
Keep the pressure of occupations and attacks visible.
shortened: 'Abdu'l-Baha was in the land of Egypt and had absolutely no opportunity for writing or speech. The distractions were endless and the attacks of enemies beyond measure.

order.why: Consider the change of plans in response to an unwelcome reception.
Read the instruction for temporary discretion as situated advice.
shortened: The point is that the friends must maintain complete silence for some days, and if anyone asks, they should express complete ignorance, so that the murmuring and rumors may subside somewhat and I may be able to come to Egypt and meet with certain important persons, for wisdom now requires this.

order.why: Preserve the reported account of visits and unannounced departure.
shortened: For nearly one month 'Abdul-Baha remained in Port Said and the friends of God came from Cairo, in turn, to visit him. One day he called me to accompany him when taking a walk in the streets of the city.
The day that he left for Alexandria he did not mention the matter to anyone; nor did this servant know the time of his departure.

order.why: Notice the practical arrangements that sustain correspondence.
shortened: O servant of the Most Glorious Beauty!

Your letter dated the fifth of Sha'ban of this year, which you had written to Aqa Siyyid Asadu'llah, was reviewed. For several days I have been staying in Ramleh of Alexandria, and day and night I am occupied with thoughts of the divine friends. Henceforth send letters directly to Port Said in care of Jenab-i-Aqa Ahmad Yazdi - wherever we may be, he will forward them.

order.why: Read the note about delay in sending a letter.
shortened: Written in Alexandria. Until now it was delayed in sending due to the press of occupations.

order.why: Compare the opportunities to write in different places.
Retain the intention to make up for missed correspondence.
Return to remembrance of friends day and night.
Recounts recovery during service, return to Alexandria, the winter in Egypt and departure for America.
Read the message of safe arrival and continuing concern.
shortened: O honored lady!
Praise be to God, by His grace we arrived safe and sound in Port Said, and we are constantly thinking of you and seeking divine assistance and confirmation.

order.why: Consider companionship and joy in a visit.
Keep the reported link between Alexandria, pilgrimage, and Port Said.
shortened: Because first you were with me in Alexandria, then you departed to visit the Holy Tomb of Baha'u'llah and now we are gathered in Port Said.

order.why: Retain the reported refusal of a photographic request.
Read the reported proposed meeting with the Khedive within the limits of the surviving wording.
shortened: When I was in Alexandria, Ahmad Ariss, the Minister of [one word cut off] of the Khedivial Court called upon me and proposed to me that he would like to arrange a meeting between his Highness the Khedive and myself.

order.why: Consider the conditional plan for another visit.
Retain the brief return from Europe with its supplied omission.
Read the intention to return and meet friends.
shortened: God willing, after teaching in these regions I will return to Alexandria and meet with the friends. If we remain alive we will mend the garment that has been torn by separation.

order.why: Consider the hope for renewed activity among the friends.
Hear the reported resolve to travel again after arranging affairs.
Place that resolve beside the modest estimate of service accomplished.
End with the prayer that strangers become friends.
shortened: O true friend! Now 'Abdu'l-Baha is in the city of Alexandria, occupied with thoughts of the friends, and night and day, in utmost lowliness and supplication, begs for confirmation and success from the threshold of the Lord of the Kingdom - that the friends may become united and agreed with one another, establishing oneness in this mortal world in such wise that every stranger may become a friend, every distant one draw near, and every outsider become an intimate.

questions: What do the letters reveal about service that a record of public events alone might miss?
How do acknowledged weakness, recovery, and determination coexist in these accounts?
What differences of purpose or circumstance should we preserve when reading the selections together?
How does Mark’s account of rest after teaching compare with the demands and pauses described here?
What quiet practices of companionship or communication might help sustain a community through changing circumstances?

neighbors.invitation: Read further recollections and accounts of a life of service.

references.label: 1 · Mark 6:30–32 · Rest amid the demands of teaching
references.note: After the apostles report what they have done and taught, Jesus invites them to withdraw and rest because the coming and going leaves little opportunity even to eat. Compare this attention to bodily limits with the letters about convalescence and renewed correspondence. The comparison concerns the demands of service, not an equivalence between the journeys.
